This prevents infinite E12 failures from corrupted manifest data. |\n696\t| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n697\t| Coding | **Fixed K=768 multi-block stream** — `blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder. Each manifest block is fountain-coded independently, inheriting the flat-cost property. |\n698\t| Cadence | Interleaved with payload on the same schedule as the beacon (D17), so a late joiner acquires it without waiting a pass |\n699\t| Before it arrives | Completed blocks are written to OPFS but tracked separately from verified blocks (two-bitmap system: `complete` for decoded, `writtenBlocks` for written). They are verified retroactively once the manifest decodes. The receiver reports \"verifying…\" rather than claiming completion. **Critical: blocks written before verification are NEVER surfaced to the user or exported until their hash is verified (I9).** |\n700\t\n701\t**Why not append the hash to each block's payload:** it would make the payload\n702\t`blockSize + 4`, breaking `blockSize = K·L` and therefore D19's entire arithmetic and G7.\n703\t\n704\t**Sizing sanity:** 21,845 blocks × 4 B = 87 KB at 4 GB ⇒ `blockCount_manifest` = 1 (one block). At 100 GB (546,125 blocks): 2.1 MB ⇒ 11 blocks. At 1 TB (5.46M blocks): 21 MB ⇒ 110 blocks. Each block decodes at K=768 (72 KB matrix), so memory stays bounded regardless of file size — flat-cost by design.\n705\t\n706\t**Why the manifest hash is mandatory:** Without it, a single flipped byte in the manifest\n707\tpacket would yield wrong hashes for hundreds of blocks. Those blocks would fail E12 forever\n708\t— re-collect, fail, re-collect — with no error code and no termination. The manifest hash\n709\tdetects this corruption immediately and forces re-decode of the manifest.\n710\t\n711\t### 7.3 Session state\n712\t\n713\t```ts\n714\ttype SendSession = {\n715\t  source: File;\n716\t  staging: FileSystemFileHandle | null;   // compressed copy (D8) — MUST be wiped\n717\t  streamId: number;\n718\t  blockSize: number; blockCount: number;\n719\t  readonly fragmentLen: number;           // L — I1\n720\t  readonly K: number;                     // D26\n721\t  cursor: { blockIndex: number; seq: number };\n722\t  dwellPackets: number;                   // §8.1\n723\t};\n724\t\n725\ttype RecvSession = {\n726\t  streamId: number | null;                // locked on first valid header\n727\t  meta: BeaconMeta | null;                // gates everything\n728\t  complete: Uint8Array;                   // block bitmap — tracks decoded blocks\n729\t  writtenBlocks: Uint8Array;              // bitmap tracking blocks written to OPFS\n730\t  active: { blockIndex: number; pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — payload block GE context\n731\t  manifestActive: { pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — manifest block GE context\n732\t  manifest: BlockHashManifest | null;    // §7.6 — persisted for resume\n733\t  out: FileSystemWritableFileStream;      // OPFS\n734\t  stats: { fps: number; cameraPxPerModule: number; packetsPerSec: number; eta: number };\n735\t};\n736\t```\n737\t\n738\t**Two-bitmap system:** `complete` tracks blocks that have been fountain-decoded; `writtenBlocks` tracks blocks that have been written to OPFS. These separate because blocks may be decoded before their hashes arrive (§7.6), and they must not be surfaced to the user until verified.\n739\t\n740\tPartial state for a block the sender has moved past is **discarded, not persisted** — a\n741\tbadly damaged block rarely half-completes usefully, and persisting it would defeat I6.\n742\tThe bitmap is tiny: 4 GB / 192 KB = 21,845 blocks = **2.7 KB**.\n743\t\n744\t### 7.4 `streamId` derivation\n745\t\n746\tLoad-bearing: D22 resume requires that re-selecting the same file reproduces the same\n747\t`streamId`, and §3.3 says a full multi-GB hash is not free.\n748\t\n749\t**Derivation (sender):**\n750\t\n751\t```\n752\tstreamId = CRC32( fileSize ‖ first 64 KB ‖ middle 64 KB ‖ last 64 KB ‖ lastModified )\n753\t```\n754\t\n755\tThree sampled windows plus size and mtime. Costs ~200 KB of reads regardless of file\n756\tsize, so it is instant even for 4 TB.\n757\t\n758\t**What this buys and what it does not:**\n759\t\n760\t- ✅ Same file re-selected → same `streamId` → resume works.\n761\t- ✅ Different files → different `streamId` with overwhelming probability.\n762\t- ⚠️ A file edited **only in the middle**, keeping size and mtime, collides. Mitigated by\n763\t  including `lastModified`, and by per-block hashes catching the mismatch at block level.\n764\t- ⚠️ This is **not** a content-integrity hash. The whole-file hash (§7.2) is, and is\n765\t  optional. `streamId` is an *identifier*.\n766\t\n767\tDeliberately **not** `crc32(payload)` — the research's original design — because the\n768\tblock layer made a full-payload pass unaffordable.\n769\t\n770\t### 7.5 Repair code format (§8.2)\n771\t\n772\tA human types this, so it must be short, unambiguous, and self-checking.\n773\t\n774\t```\n775\tSF1-<streamId36>-<ranges36>-<check>\n776\t```\n777\t\n778\t- **Alphabet:** Crockford base32 (no I/L/O/U — removes the common misreadings).\n779\t- **`ranges`:** run-length encoded missing-block set. Contiguous runs are the common case\n780\t  because misses cluster (the user looked away).\n781\t- **`check`:** 2 characters, CRC-8 over the decoded body. A mistyped code MUST be\n782\t  rejected, never acted on — acting on a corrupted range wastes hours.\n783\t- **Length bound:** if the encoded form exceeds **48 characters**, the receiver MUST\n784\t  instead offer a QR containing the same payload (which the sender's camera reads, or the\n785\t  user photographs), and say so. A 100 GB file with scattered misses can exceed any\n786\t  reasonable typing length, and silently truncating the set would be a correctness bug.\n787\t\n788\t### 7.7 Normative wire constants\n789\t\n790\tThe following constants are **fixed in code** and **MUST** be reproduced exactly by any\n791\tthird-party implementation. They are not subject to negotiation or configuration; changing\n792\tany of these is a wire-format breaking change (§16.3). These are what §14.3's conformance\n793\tvectors exist to validate.\n794\t\n795\t| Constant | Value | Purpose | Location |\n796\t|---|---|---|---|\n797\t| **MAGIC** | `0x5` | 4-bit magic in header `magic_ver` field; used for fast rejection of foreign QR symbols. The high nibble of byte 0 in every packet header. | `src/core/params.ts` |\n798\t| **WIRE_VERSION** | `1` | 4-bit wire version in header `magic_ver` field; indicates wire format revision. Packets with mismatched versions are rejected with `E-VERSION`. | `src/core/params.ts` |\n799\t| **CRC-8 polynomial** | `0x31` | CRC-8 polynomial used for `fcrc` field in packet headers (covers bytes 0–11 only). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n800\t| **CRC-8 initial value** | `0xff` | Initial CRC value for CRC-8 computation. | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n801\t| **CRC-32 polynomial** | `0xedb88320` | IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 polynomial used for `streamId` derivation (§7.4), `manifestHash` (§7.2), and `beaconCRC` (§7.2). This is the standard IEEE polynomial (reversed representation). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n802\t| **CRC-32 initial value** | `0xffffffff` | Initial CRC value for CRC-32 computation (XORed with seed, final XOR with `0xffffffff`). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n803\t| **SplitMix32 increment** | `0x9e3779b9` | Golden ratio φ = 2³²/φ, used to increment state in SplitMix32 PRNG. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n804\t| **SplitMix32 round 1 multiplier** | `0x21f0aaad` | First mixing constant in SplitMix32 avalanche. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n805\t| **SplitMix32 round 2 multiplier** | `0x735a2d97` | Second mixing constant in SplitMix32 avalanche. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n806\t| **packetSeed round 1 multiplier** | `0x85ebca6b` | First mixing constant when combining `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. **Order is normative** — changing the order of operations or the constants changes the derived index set. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n807\t| **packetSeed round 2 multiplier** | `0xc2b2ae35` | Second mixing constant when combining `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n808\t| **Partial Fisher-Yates algorithm** | Fisher-Yates shuffle truncated at `d` iterations | Generates `d` distinct indices from `[0, k)` without rejection sampling. Critical for bounded-time index derivation. The algorithm is: (1) initialize `pool[i] = i` for `i in [0, k)`, (2) for `i in [0, d)`: `j = i + floor(rnd() * (k - i))`, swap `pool[i]` and `pool[j]`, return `pool[i]`. **This exact algorithm is normative** — any change produces different index sets. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n809\t\n810\t**Implementation notes:**\n811\t\n812\t- All CRC implementations use the standard definitions: CRC-8 uses polynomial `0x31` (ITU-T I.432.1 / ATM HEC) with initial value `0xff`; CRC-32 uses the IEEE 802.3 polynomial with initial/final XOR `0xffffffff`.\n813\t- SplitMix32 is a simple PRNG sufficient for fountain code index selection. The constants shown are the standard ones from the algorithm's definition.\n814\t- `packetSeed` mixes three 32-bit values (streamId, blockIndex, seq) into one 32-bit seed for SplitMix32. The exact mixing order and constants are **normative** — a different implementation must produce identical output for the same inputs, or index sets will not match and fountain decoding will fail.\n815\t- The partial Fisher-Yates shuffle is critical: it produces exactly `d` distinct indices in `[0, k)` with O(d) time and O(k) space. A naïve rejection-sampling approach would have unbounded time and is **forbidden**.\n816\t\n817\t**Conformance testing:** §14.3 requires test vectors covering `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` to validate the entire PRNG chain (packetSeed → SplitMix32 → partial Fisher-Yates). Any implementation change to the constants or algorithms above breaks these vectors and is a wire-format violation.\n818\t\n819\t---\n820\t\n821\t## 8. Behaviour at gigabyte scale\n822\t\n823\t### 8.1 Block scheduling and the dwell budget\n824\t\n825\tThe sender does not know which blocks the receiver has, so it dwells on each block for\n826\t`dwellPackets`, then advances, looping the file continuously.\n827\t\n828\t**Dwell must survive the top of the assumed erasure band.** An earlier revision paired\n829\tdwell 1.4 K with a 20–30% band, which failed at the top of its own band — at 30%\n830\terasure, 1.4 K delivers 0.98 K against the ~1.02 K needed, so **every block missed its\n831\tfirst pass**, each costing a full extra pass.\n832\t\n833\tThe fix is to raise dwell, **not** to narrow the band. Narrowing it (a briefly-adopted\n834\tmistake) contradicts the evidence base, which specifies 20–30% and warns that driving\n835\terasure lower means the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused.\n836\t\n837\t| dwell | 20% erasure | 25% | **30%** | needed |\n838\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n839\t| 1.4 K | 1.120 K | 1.050 K | **0.980 K ❌** | ~1.02 K |\n840\t| **1.6 K** | 1.280 K | 1.200 K | **1.120 K ✅** | ~1.02 K |\n841\t\n842\t- **dwell = 1.6 × K** (default; tunable)\n843\t- **assumed band = 20–30%** (D18c) — an assumption, not a controlled target\n844\t\n845\tA test MUST assert `dwell × (1 − erasure_max) ≥ 1.12`, matching §13.1's +12% p99\n846\toverhead budget, so dwell and the band cannot drift apart again.\n847\t\n848\t**The e_max completion cliff.** A block completes on a pass iff `dwell × (1 − e) ≥ 1 + overhead`.\n849\tAt dwell 1.6 K and the measured +2.97% mean overhead (§13.1):\n850\t```\n851\te_max = 1 − 1.0297 / 1.6 = 35.6%\n852\t```\n853\tAbove this erasure rate, every pass delivers **less than K independent packets** — the block\n854\tnever reaches full rank, the decoder resets, and the next pass starts from rank 0. **The transfer\n855\tNEVER FINISHES**, at any file size, with the progress bar frozen at zero blocks. This is why the\n856\trepair code (§8.2) exists: when real erasure exceeds e_max, human mediation is the designed recovery path.\n857\t\n858\t**When real erasure exceeds 30%** — which nothing in v1 can detect (D18a) — blocks miss\n859\tand the **repair code (§8.2) is the recovery path**, not a tighter loop. This is the\n860\tdesigned answer, not a gap.\n861\t\n862\t**Dwell is a standing ~60% overhead.** The sender always emits 1.6× what a block needs,\n863\twhatever the channel. §13.1's throughput budgets are stated **after** this factor —\n864\tthey are goodput, not wire rate.\n865\t\n866\t### 8.2 Human-mediated repair — the cheap back-channel\n867\t\n868\tThe receiver knows exactly which blocks it lacks. The user reads a code off one screen and\n869\ttypes it into the other:\n870\t\n871\t> **Receiver:** \"Missing 3 blocks. Repair code: `SF1-K7F2M9-3B-X4`\"\n872\t> **Sender:** [paste] → transmits only those blocks\n873\t\n874\tTurns a multi-hour extra pass into a sub-minute repair, needs no second camera and no\n875\tgeometry constraints, and is what makes small blocks (§3.4) affordable. Format: §7.5.\n876\t\n877\t### 8.3 Resume (D22)\n878\t\n879\tThe receiver persists `{streamId, meta, complete, writtenBlocks, manifest}` plus the OPFS output after every completed\n880\tblock. On reload it offers to resume. At 2.7 KB per 4 GB for the bitmaps this is nearly free; the manifest adds\n881\t87 KB for a 4 GB file (21,845 blocks × 4-byte hashes). **The manifest MUST be persisted** — without it,\n882\tresume cannot re-verify blocks, and a reload during the ~12 minute manifest acquisition window would lose\n883\tall received blocks.\n884\t\n885\tThe sender is stateless across restarts by construction (D24) **when compression is disabled** —\n886\tit needs only the same file and the same `streamId` (§7.4). **With compression enabled, resume is\n887\tNOT supported** — see `docs/notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md` for the full analysis,\n888\t`docs/notes/bf-3k90-compression-resume-solution-evaluation.md` for the solution evaluation,\n889\tand `notes/bf-2w1a.md` for validation and test coverage.\n890\tThe short version: `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after\n891\tstaging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state.\n892\tThe beacon carries a `ResumeDisabled` flag (beacon `flags` field) when compression is on;\n893\tthe receiver uses this flag to suppress resume UI and prevent persisting resume tokens.\n894\tThis preserves the T4 privacy requirement (staging is still wiped on startup) while preventing\n895\tsilent corruption.\n896\t\n897\t**On resume the receiver MUST re-verify block hashes** rather than trusting the bitmap, in\n898\tcase OPFS was corrupted or the file was touched externally. This requires the manifest to be\n899\tpersisted alongside the bitmap.\n900\t\n901\t**Pre-manifest reload behavior:** If the receiver is reloaded before the manifest arrives\n902\t(e.g., during the ~12 minute acquisition window for a 4 GB file at the beacon's ~2 s cadence),\n903\tthe persisted bitmap preserves which blocks were decoded, and the written blocks remain in OPFS.\n904\tThe `writtenBlocks` bitmap is reset on resume, and blocks are re-verified once the manifest arrives.\n905\tThis prevents losing all received blocks during the manifest acquisition window.\n906\t\n907\t### 8.4 Storage limits\n908\t\n909\t| Platform | Practical quota |\n910\t|---|---|\n911\t| Chrome / Edge desktop | ~60% of free disk — multi-GB fine |\n912\t| Firefox | ~10% of disk (capped ~10 GB) |\n913\t| **Safari / iOS** | **~1 GB** before prompting; expandable but user-gated |\n914\t\n915\t**Multi-GB reception is a desktop-Chromium story.** The app MUST query\n916\t`navigator.storage.estimate()` up front and refuse clearly (§13.1) rather than failing at\n917\thour 9. With compression on, staging needs the compressed size *plus* the output.\n918\t\n919\t---\n920\t\n921\t## 9. Acceptance scenarios\n922\t\n923\tNamed, independently verifiable, with explicit pass **and fail** criteria. \"Fail\" means\n924\tstop and reconsider the design, not retry.\n925\t\n926\t| # | Scenario | Setup | Action | Pass | Fail |\n927\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n928\t| **A1** | Small file, ideal conditions | Laptop (1080p, 50% brightness min) → Pixel-class phone, 30 cm, office lighting (~300 lux), tripod | Send a 1 MB binary file (random bytes, incompressible) | Byte-identical output; ≥ 20 KB/s sustained; completes in ≤ 60 s | < 10 KB/s, or any byte differs |\n929\t| **A1-lite** | Byte-exactness on two real devices | Two real devices (any configuration) | Send any file | Byte-identical output | Any byte differs |\n930\t| **A2** | Handheld, realistic | As A1 but handheld, receiver held **portrait** (the default, unassisted grip — §6.3.2) | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≥ 10 KB/s | Does not complete in 5 min |\n931\t| **A3** | Phone → phone | Two phones, 15 cm, handheld | Send 100 KB | Byte-identical; completes in ≤ 5 min | Does not complete — triggers §18 R4 |\n932\t| **A4** | Lossy channel | A1 setup; camera deliberately occluded 30% of the time in 2-second bursts | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≤ 1.6× the A1 frame count | > 3× A1 frame count (fountain code is not delivering) |\n933\t| **A5** | Large file, memory flat | Desktop Chromium, synthetic 4 GB stream, headless block layer | Full encode→decode at the block layer | Byte-identical; peak heap ≤ 1 MB (I6a); no growth trend across 21,800 blocks | Any monotonic memory growth |\n934\t| **A6** | Resume | A1 setup, 10 MB file | Reload the receiver tab at ~50% | Offers resume; completes; byte-identical | Restarts from zero, or completes with wrong bytes |\n935\t| **A7** | Repair | A1 setup, 10 MB file, 5 blocks deliberately dropped | Enter the repair code on the sender | Only the missing blocks retransmit; completes in < 60 s | Full pass required |\n936\t| **A8** | Offline | Both devices in airplane mode, app previously loaded | Full A1 transfer | Completes normally | Any network request attempted (asserted by CI, §14.4) |\n937\t| **A9** | Wrong stream | Two senders visible in frame | Receiver points at both | Locks one `streamId`, ignores the other, says so | Mixes packets from both |\n938\t| **A10** | Hostile beacon | Crafted beacon declaring `originalSize` = 281 TB | Receiver parses it | Refuses with `E-META-BOUNDS`; no allocation attempted | Allocates or crashes |\n939\t\n940\t**Adoption metrics are deliberately absent.** With no backend and no telemetry there is no\n941\tway to measure them, and the ledger consciously cut the voluntary-benchmark idea. This is a\n942\tstated limitation, not an oversight — see §18 R8.\n943\t\n944\t---\n945\t\n946\t## 10. Edge case catalog\n947\t\n948\t| # | Case | Resolution |\n949\t|---|---|---|\n950\t| E1 | **Zero-byte file** | Reject at selection with a clear message. `K = 0` is undefined. |\n951\t| E2 | **File smaller than one fragment** (< 256 B) | Pad to one fragment; `K = 1`; the fountain code degenerates to repetition, which is correct. Research specifies a `K < 8` guard — adopt it: below 8 fragments, send plain repetition, no LT. **Repetition is derived per-block** (not signalled): both encoder and decoder derive `repetition = (k < MIN_LT_K)` from the block's K using the shared per-block derivation E3a already mandates. A session-wide flag would force repetition on all 21,845 blocks or none; per-block derivation allows the last block (K=1-7) to use repetition while all other blocks (K=768) use LT. |\n952\t| E3a | **The last block is short** — its K is `ceil(lastLen / L)`, not 768. Both sides derive K per block, and D7's PRNG is seeded with it. A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, payloadLen)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. The beacon's `payloadLen` field (§7.2) is critical — without it, the receiver cannot compute the last block's actual length (`lastLen = payloadLen − (blockCount − 1) × blockSize`), leading to PRNG index mismatch and silent decode failure. |\n953\t| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n954\t| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. |\n955\t| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n956\t| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n957\t| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n958\t| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n959\t| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never discard collected blocks. |\n960\t| E10 | **OPFS quota exhausted mid-transfer** | Stop, keep completed blocks, export a partial file plus a manifest of what is missing. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n961\t| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. Also a privacy requirement (§12, T4a). |\n962\t| E12 | **Block hash verification fails** | After manifest arrives, block hash verification fails. Clear the verified bitmap bit, re-collect the block. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. Block may already be written to OPFS but is never surfaced until verified (I9). This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n963\t| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n964\t| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n965\t| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`; keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost. **The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n966\t| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. |\n967\t| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. |\n968\t| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** and drop decode resolution. |\n969\t| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer, do not silently restart. |\n970\t\n971\t---\n972\t\n973\t## 11. Error taxonomy\n974\t\n975\tEvery distinguishable condition gets a stable code and one user-facing sentence. Defined\n976\tnow, before Phase 5 designs any UI — after that, taxonomies get retrofitted to screens.\n977\t\n978\t**Optical / acquisition** (the stall detector's job, `bf-5vm`):\n979\t\n980\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n981\t|---|---|---|\n982\t| `E-NO-SIGNAL` | No decodable tiles at all | \"Point the camera at the sending screen.\" |\n983\t| `E-TOO-FAR` | **camera** px/module < 4 (§2) | \"Move closer — the code is too small to read.\" |\n984\t| `E-TOO-CLOSE` | Symbol exceeds frame, or below min focus | \"Move back a little.\" |\n985\t| `E-BLUR` | Sharpness metric below threshold | \"Hold steady.\" |\n986\t| `E-DARK` | Insufficient exposure | \"Too dark — raise the sender's screen brightness.\" |\n987\t| `E-GLARE` | Saturated region over the code | \"Tilt to avoid the reflection.\" |\n988\t| `E-FOCUS-HUNT` | Focus oscillating | \"Tap the screen to lock focus.\" |\n989\t| `E-ORIENTATION` | Detected capture aspect doesn't match the sender's configured setting (§6.3.2) — e.g. sender is shaping the code for landscape but the receiver is held portrait | \"This app works fine held normally — but if you'd like more margin, match the orientation setting on the sending device, or turn the phone sideways.\" (tip, not a blocker — portrait is fully supported) |\n990\t| `E-SENDER-STALLED` | Identical frames repeating | \"The sending device seems paused.\" |\n991\t| `E-TORN` | Torn-frame rate high | \"Lower the sender's frame rate.\" |\n992\t\n993\t**Protocol:**\n994\t\n995\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n996\t|---|---|---|---|\n997\t| `E-FOREIGN-STREAM` | Different `streamId` (E7) | \"That's a different file — ignoring it.\" | automatic, informational |\n998\t| `E-VERSION` | Unknown `magic_ver` (§16.3) | \"The sending device is running version X; this one is Y. Update both.\" | user must update |\n999\t| `E-META-BOUNDS` | Beacon field out of bounds (T1) | \"That transmission looks malformed and was rejected.\" | automatic, refuse |\n1000\t| `E-MANIFEST-CORRUPT` | Manifest CRC validation failed (§7.6) | \"The block manifest is corrupted and is being re-decoded.\" | automatic retry |\n1001\t| `E-MANIFEST-MISSING` | Manifest never arrived (§7.6) | \"Waiting for block manifest to verify received chunks.\" | wait or request repair |\n1002\t| `E-MANIFEST-DECODE` | Manifest fountain decode failed (§7.6) | \"Could not decode the block manifest. Retrying...\" | automatic retry |\n1003\t| `E-MANIFEST-LIVELOCK` | E12 livelock detected, manifest corrupted (bf-5fm) | \"Multiple chunks failed verification — the manifest appears corrupted. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1004\t| `E-BLOCK-HASH` | Rank K reached, hash failed (E12) | \"A chunk arrived corrupted and is being re-collected.\" | automatic retry |\n1005\t| `E-BLOCK-RETRY-EXCEEDED` | Block retry limit exceeded (E12 livelock, bf-5fm) | \"A chunk has failed verification too many times. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n1006\t| `E-K-OVERFLOW` | Sender K exceeds receiver's maximum (D26) | \"Sender's chunk size is too large for this device. Use a smaller file or a more powerful receiver.\" | refuse, user adjusts |\n1007\t| `E-REPAIR-BOUNDS` | Repair code references blocks beyond file (§8.2) | \"That repair code refers to chunks that don't exist. Check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1008\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1009\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n1010\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n1011\t\n1012\t**Status codes** (informational, not errors):\n1013\t\n1014\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n1015\t|---|---|---|\n1016\t| `E-VERIFYING` | Verifying blocks against manifest (§7.6) | \"Verifying received chunks against manifest...\" |\n1017\t\n1018\t**Local / resource:**\n1019\t\n1020\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n1021\t|---|---|---|---|\n1022\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n1023\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n1024\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n1025\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n1026\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n1027\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n1028\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n1029\t\n1030\t---\n1031\t\n1032\t## 12. Threat model\n1033\t\n1034\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n1035\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n1036\t\n1037\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n1038\t|---|---|---|---|\n1039\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `originalSize` and `payloadLen` (281 TB each), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `originalSize` ≤ available quota, `payloadLen` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n1040\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n1041\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `originalSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n1042\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n1043\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n1044\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash).
