So its advantage is **both** density and frame\n1208\trate, and Stage 3 is *more* attractive than the corrected-away version suggested — not less.\n1209\t\n1210\tWhat survives from that reasoning: **decode CPU per bit is the metric that matters**, and the\n1211\tcheap decode-side wins (worker pool, tight ROI, capture resolution, D27) come first because\n1212\tthey are cheap, not because symbology is worthless. **R7 (MPL-2.0 licensing) and §19 Q1 are\n1213\ttherefore NOT de-urgentised** — they gate Phase 7 and Phase 7 is worth reaching.\n1214\t\n1215\t**The dominant risk is geometry, not software.** Cell size is set by how many *camera\n1216\tpixels* the sender's screen occupies:\n1217\t\n1218\t- Laptop → phone at 30 cm: ~1325 px across ≈ 165-cell grid\n1219\t- **Phone → phone: ~327 px across ≈ 54 cells — one ninth the capacity**\n1220\t\n1221\tPhone→phone is also bounded by **minimum focus distance**: filling the frame needs ~6.6 cm,\n1222\tinside the ~10 cm focus limit, so the symbol spans only 50–60% of frame.\n1223\t\n1224\t---\n1225\t\n1226\t## 16. Platform and operations\n1227\t\n1228\t### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n1229\t\n1230\t- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n1231\t- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n1232\t  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n1233\t  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n1234\t- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n1235\t  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n1236\t- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n1237\t- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n1238\t- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n1239\t  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n1240\t- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n1241\t  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n1242\t- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n1243\t- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n1244\t\n1245\t### 16.2 Deployment\n1246\t\n1247\tStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\n1248\tNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n1249\t**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n1250\t\n1251\t### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n1252\t\n1253\tTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\n1254\ta service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\n1255\tbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n1256\t\n1257\t| Rule | |\n1258\t|---|---|\n1259\t| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n1260\t| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n1261\t| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n1262\t| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n1263\t| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n1264\t| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n1265\t| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n1266\t\n1267\t### 16.4 Health check\n1268\t\n1269\tOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\n1270\tthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\n1271\tlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n1272\t**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n1273\t\n1274\t---\n1275\t\n1276\t## 17. Phases\n1277\t\n1278\tEach phase has **entry criteria** (what must be green before starting) and **exit\n1279\tcriteria** (testable). Phases 1–3 are the critical path; the parallel track can proceed\n1280\tindependently once Phase 0 lands.\n1281\t\n1282\t| Phase | Entry | Exit |\n1283\t|---|---|---|\n1284\t| **0 — Repo and harness** ⚠️ *partial* | — | Builds, deploys, version footer present, stub-camera tier runs, G1–G3 and **G7** green, **module layout (§6.5) and dependency pins committed**, and a throwaway end-to-end spike (one tiny file through a no-op modulation) proves the seams line up |\n1285\t| **0.5 — Spike** ⚠️ *partial* | Phase 0 exit | S1–S4 run and recorded in `docs/notes/spike-results.md`; §13.1's forecast rows replaced with measured figures or the relevant §18 risk triggered. **Gates Phase 1 because it sets K, L, dwell and the rung ladder.** See `spike/README.md` |\n1286\t| **1 — Core codec, headless** ⚠️ *built, gates unmet* | Phase 0.5 exit | 10 MB file survives 50% loss byte-exact; overhead within `sim/` bounds; synthetic 4 GB at flat ≤ 1 MB (A5 / I6a); GE keeps pace at K=768 measured on a real phone; G1–G5 green |\n1287\t| **2 — Single-QR optical loop — the walking skeleton** | Phase 1 exit | **A1-lite passes** (byte-exactness on two real devices, no throughput floor). **This is the first demonstrable end-to-end transfer**; Phase 0's spike is a seam check, not a product |\n1288\t| **3 — Tiling + fixed-weight ladder (D18a)** | Phase 2 exit | A1 ≥ 20 KB/s, A2, A3, A4 pass on T-physical-rig; G6 green |\n1289\t| **4 — Large-file machinery** | Phase 3 exit | A5, A6, A7, A10 pass; quota pre-flight refuses correctly; repair code round-trips |\n1290\t| **5 — The app + local ladder adaptation (D18b)** | Phase 4 exit | A8, A9 pass; every §11 error code has a user-facing string and is reachable; iOS manual pass; non-technical user completes a transfer unaided |\n1291\t| **6 — Calibration probe + colour** | Phase 5 exit | Probe reports device cutoffs; colour enabled only where it measurably wins; A1 improves or colour stays off |\n1292\t| **7 — Custom codec** | Phase 6 exit **and** the §19 Q1 licensing decision recorded | Stage 3 beats Stage 2 on T-physical-rig |\n1293\t\n1294\t### 17.2 Where the phases actually stand — and the gates that were skipped\n1295\t\n1296\tRecorded honestly, because a gate that reads green and is not is how Phase 3 inherits Phase 0's\n1297\tdebt (PIVOT-CAUSES PH-2).\n1298\t\n1299\t| Phase | Claimed | Reality |\n1300\t|---|---|---|\n1301\t| 0 | partial | **Exit criteria NOT met.** `npm run build` fails (no `index.html`, no `src/app.ts`); no version footer (`bf-13h` open); no stub-camera tier; **no lint config**, so G1 cannot pass; G2 (no-network assertion) and G3 (bundle budget, SRI) unimplemented. **G7 is green.** `npm run gate` currently runs typecheck + tests + G7 — a subset of G1 plus G7. |\n1302\t| 0.5 | partial | S1, S2, S3 and the thermal observation done. **Outstanding:** phone→phone (R4), rung sweep, a distance sweep under §13.2 conditions, an on-device GE run, and the long-run thermal profile. Its exit criterion — \"§13.1's forecast rows replaced with measured figures\" — is now met for three rows (§13.1). |\n1303\t| 1 | built, **exit criteria NOT met** | `src/core/` has framing, PRNG, LT encode, GE decode, block layer; 22 tests green. **Unmet:** G1–G3 (inherited from Phase 0); the A5 memory assertion is a smoke test, not I6a; the **on-device GE run** required by \"GE keeps pace at K=768 measured on a real phone\" has not happened. **Not yet written** (listed in §6.5): `frame/beacon.ts`, `frame/repair-code.ts`, `hash/block-hash.ts`, `hash/stream-id.ts`, `block/schedule.ts`. **I3's golden vector `test/fixtures/vectors.json` does not exist** (AP10 is live, not paid-for). Entered on a partial 0.5, so K, L, dwell and the rung ladder shipped at their modelled values. |\n1304\t\n1305\t**Gate defects to close before Phase 2:**\n1306\t\n1307\t0. **The `zxing-wasm` CDN default (§6.5) must be overridden and the `.wasm` precached** — as\n1308\t   shipped it would make a network request mid-session and fail offline entirely.\n1309\t\n1310\t1. **Phase 0's harness must be built or §17 amended.** Do not leave the discrepancy implicit.\n1311\t2. **The on-device GE benchmark has not run**, and D26/T1 both cite a \"locally benchmarked max\" that no component produces (§16.4 owns it).\n1312\t3. **The A5 memory assertion is a smoke test, not the invariant.** `test/codec.test.ts` checks a\n1313\t   heap *trend* with 64 MB of slack across 40 blocks (7.9 MB), which cannot detect a 40 MB\n1314\t   working set and does not approach I6a's ≤ 1 MB over 21,800 blocks.\n1315\t\n1316\t**Process gap this exposes.** `spike-results.md` ended with a section titled \"Plan changes this\n1317\tjustifies\" listing five; none was applied until a review caught it. §14.6 requires the plan be\n1318\tupdated \"if any decision changed\" — but a **measurement** is not a **decision**, so nothing\n1319\ttriggered. **Rule: any spike or hardware measurement MUST be folded into §13.1, §18 and the\n1320\trevision history in the same commit that records it.** Owner: whoever runs the measurement.\n1321\t\n1322\t### 17.1 Phase 0.5 — why a spike, and why here\n1323\t\n1324\tThe plan's parameters are currently modelled or borrowed from research on other\n1325\tpeople's hardware. The spike does not decide **whether** to build the codec — the\n1326\tfountain code, block layer and framing are needed whatever the channel does. It\n1327\tdecides **what numbers to build it with**, and those numbers are encoded in the\n1328\tframing layer that Phase 1 writes:\n1329\t\n1330\t| Parameter | Basis today | Sets |\n1331\t|---|---|---|\n1332\t| Tiling gain (~10×) | measured on *simulated* camera paths | D1, the throughput thesis |\n1333\t| Erasure 20–30% | **assumption** (D18c states this) | dwell = 1.6 K (§8.1) |\n1334\t| 4 px/module cliff | other devices | D2, §3.1.1's rungs, `bf-1g0` |\n1335\t| Delivered fps | a Pixel 6, not ours | D9, D14 |\n1336\t| 200 MB/s JS XOR | ~~unmeasured guess~~ **measured: 3,260 MB/s desktop (S1)** | D19's K = 768 |\n1337\t\n1338\tIt is cheap *precisely because* it skips everything this plan carefully designs: no\n1339\tfountain code, no blocks, no compression, no resume, no OPFS, no UI. Sequential\n1340\tnumbered packets and a counter suffice — the subject is the channel, not the protocol.\n1341\t\n1342\t**S1 is already done** (`spike/ge-bench.mjs`, no camera or install needed). A full\n1343\tGE decode of one block at K = 768 takes **8 ms** at **3,260 MB/s** on the dev\n1344\tmachine — the 200 MB/s budget was ~16× pessimistic, leaving **7.1× margin at\n1345\tStage 3** even after a harsh ÷4 phone factor. **R1 is provisionally closed**, pending\n1346\ta re-run in a browser on the target phone; the ÷4 factor is itself a guess.\n1347\t\n1348\tS2–S4 (rung sweep, distance sweep, handheld and phone→phone) need the optical rig and\n1349\ttwo devices. Kill criteria are fixed in advance in `spike/README.md`, each mapping to\n1350\tan existing §18 risk — if a criterion trips, the named risk's fallback applies rather\n1351\tthan an improvised one.\n1352\t\n1353\t**Do not let spike code become product code.** Separate directory, separate\n1354\t`package.json`, deleted once the results land.\n1355\t\n1356\t**Parallel track** (independent of the codec, may run alongside Phases 1–3): PWA shell,\n1357\tservice worker, file in/out per platform, pairing splash (`bf-4tb`), version footer\n1358\t(`bf-13h`), photosensitivity work (`bf-6d3`). **Sync point:** must merge before Phase 5.\n1359\t\n1360\t**Scope estimate.** Fountain + GE ≈ 300 lines (corroborated by research). Block layer,\n1361\tframing, session ≈ 800. Modulation Stage 1 ≈ 600. Receiver pipeline ≈ 700. App shell, UI,\n1362\tcoaching ≈ 1500 — **Phase 5 is the largest single phase**, which the phase ordering hides.\n1363\t\n1364\t---\n1365\t\n1366\t## 18. Risk register\n1367\t\n1368\t| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Trigger → fallback |\n1369\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n1370\t| **R1** | **GE still too slow at K=768 on real phones** | ~~Medium~~ **Low** | High — blocks Phase 1 | Cost model + conservative K (D19/D26). **S1 measured 3,260 MB/s desktop = 7.1× margin at Stage 3 after a ÷4 phone factor; provisionally closed pending an on-device re-run** | Measured need > budget → drop to K=512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 against wirehair/RaptorQ (whose linear-time decode is what libcimbar uses) |\n1371\t| **R2** | **4 camera px/module cliff makes handheld use impractical** | Medium | High | **Sender shapes the code region to the receiver's portrait aspect by default (§6.3.2) — clears the cliff without any user action.** Aim reticle + coach (`bf-1g0`), ladder (D16) as secondary aids | A2 fails → mandate a stand in the UI and reposition as a mounted-device tool |\n1372\t| **R3** | **Stage 1 measures far below 20 KB/s** | Medium | High — undermines the multi-GB objective | Tiling (D1) is the measured 10× | < 10 KB/s → cap the advertised file size, move Stage 2 earlier |\n1373\t| **R4** | **Phone→phone unusable at 54 cells** | **High** | Medium | Separate profile with bigger modules | A3 fails → document phone→phone as a small-file-only mode |\n1374\t| **R5** | **iOS cannot export multi-GB** | **High** | Medium | Detect and cap up front | `share()` fails > 1 GB → iOS is receive-capped, stated at file selection |\n1375\t| **R6** | **OPFS quota smaller than advertised** | Medium | Medium | Pre-flight (`bf-4d6`) + graceful stop (E10) | Repeated E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED → lower the refuse threshold |\n1376\t| **R7** | **libcimbar MPL-2.0 contaminates the licence** | Low | Medium | Decide before Phase 7 (§19 Q1) | Cannot accept mixed licence → clean-room Stage 3 or stop at Stage 2 |\n1377\t| **R8** | **No way to learn real-world performance** (no telemetry by design) | **High** | Low | Accepted; T-physical-rig substitutes | If field failures are suspected → voluntary copyable benchmark string (ledger, currently cut) |\n1378\t| **R9** | **Multi-hour transfers die to backgrounding / sleep / thermal** | **High** | Medium | E8, E17, wake lock, resume (D22) | Resume proves insufficient → reduce block size further so less is lost |\n1379\t| **R10** | **A wire-version bump strands cached receivers** | Medium | Medium | §16.3 one-way-door rule | Skew observed → extend the soak period before bumping |\n1380\t| **R12** | **Residual erasure exceeds the assumed 20–30% band** | **High** — measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | **High** — D18c, the §8.1 dwell budget and every §13.1 throughput figure rest on this band | Raise dwell; promote the repair code (§8.2). Note v1 cannot *observe* erasure (D18a), so this is an assumption, not a controlled quantity | Erasure > 35% under §13.2 conditions → the **repair code becomes the primary recovery path, not the tail**, and dwell is re-derived from the measured band |\n1381\t| **R11** | **Thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating** | **High** (observed first session) | **High** — attacks the multi-GB objective directly | Duty-cycling (D27), decode-resolution drop, resume (D22). Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | Sustained fps decline > 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and **tell the user**, rather than silently running hot and slow. If duty-cycling cannot hold the rate, reframe multi-GB as a multi-session workflow (§1.1) |\n1382\t\n1383\t---\n1384\t\n1385\t## 18.1 Anti-patterns — mistakes this project has already made\n1386\t\n1387\tEvery entry below was made *in this repo* and cost real time. They are collected here because\n1388\teach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\n1389\tstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n1390\t\n1391\t| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n1392\t|---|---|---|---|\n1393\t| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n1394\t| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n1395\t| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n1396\t| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n1397\t| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n1398\t| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n1399\t| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n1400\t| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n1401\t| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n1402\t| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n1403\t\n1404\t## 18.2 Proof obligations\n1405\t\n1406\tEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\n1407\tbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n1408\t2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n1409\t\n1410\t| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n1411\t|---|---|---|---|\n1412\t| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n1413\t| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n1414\t| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n1415\t| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n1416\t| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n1417\t| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n1418\t| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n1419\t\n1420\t## 19. Open questions\n1421\t\n1422\t1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n1423\t   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Porting is legal but makes the repo\n1424\t   mixed-license and obliges per-file marking. The failure mode is someone pasting in a\n1425\t   function and deciding this by accident. → [`prior-art-libcimbar.md`](../notes/prior-art-libcimbar.md)\n1426\t2. **Optimal K and block size on real hardware.** §3.1 is a model, not a measurement.\n1427\t   Resolve in Phase 1 (R1).\n1428\t3. **Phone→phone viability** at 54 cells. Resolve in Phase 3 (R4).\n1429\t4. **Progress UX with no back-channel.** The sender cannot know receiver progress. Over a\n1430\t   10-hour transfer this matters far more than over 30 seconds. **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1431\t5. **Should the sender ever stop?** It loops forever; at GB scale \"forever\" may be days.\n1432\t   **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1433\t6. **Delta transfer vs fixed blocks** — see §20.2. **Resolve before Phase 4 implementation.**\n1434\t7. **Closed-loop negotiation — deferred on evidence.** Bidirectional links are precedented\n1435\t   (MAMBA: two phones, 11–28 kbps each way), but MAMBA's measured gain from closing the\n1436\t   loop is only **5–20%**, while changing the coding paradigm buys multiples. Reassess\n1437\t   after Phase 4. → [`link-adaptation-design.md`](../notes/link-adaptation-design.md)\n1438\t8. **SoftLight-style soft hints — the highest-ceiling idea we are not doing.** Per-bit\n1439\t   confidence plus a false-positive-tolerant rateless code: **2.2× with fixed parameters**.\n1440\t   Blocked on zxing returning hard bytes; natural fit for Stage 3.\n1441\t9. **Multi-GB export on iOS** (R5). Detect up front, never at hour 9.\n1442\t10. **Encryption.** Out of scope for v1 (T6), but the optical channel is uniquely exposed\n1443\t    to filming. Revisit once transport is real.\n1444\t\n1445\t---\n1446\t\n1447\t## 20. Adopted roadmap items\n1448\t\n1449\tFrom [`ideas-ledger.md`](../notes/ideas-ledger.md) (103 generated → 10 finalists → 7\n1450\tadopted). Tracked as beads blocking genesis `bf-28p`.\n1451\t\n1452\t| Bead | Item | Grade | Phase |\n1453\t|---|---|---|---|\n1454\t| `bf-4d6` | Storage pre-flight and capacity gate | S | 4 |\n1455\t| `bf-5vm` | Diagnostic stall detector | M | 5 |\n1456\t| `bf-1g0` | Aim reticle and distance coach | M | 5 |\n1457\t| `bf-6d3` | Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1) | S | 5 |\n1458\t| `bf-280` | Delta transfer and cross-session resume | L | 4+ |\n1459\t| `bf-4tb` | Pairing splash QR | S | 5 |\n1460\t| `bf-13h` | Verifiable build + version footer | M | 0 |\n1461\t\n1462\t**Rejected:** *text/secret fast path* (a different product inside this one) and\n1463\t*single-file HTML build* (deploying as a static site, and WASM is required — exactly what\n1464\tsingle-file cannot cleanly inline). The PWA offline story is unaffected.\n1465\t\n1466\t### 20.1 Photosensitivity changes a rendering decision (`bf-6d3`)\n1467\t\n1468\tWCAG 2.3.1 caps general flashes at three per second **or** requires the flashing area to\n1469\tstay under the small-safe threshold. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\n1470\thours is a genuine seizure risk.\n1471\t\n1472\t**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\n1473\tfewer cells → less throughput. The compliant design is therefore **a bounded coded region\n1474\tinside a static surround**, not full-bleed, and the area cost MUST be measured in Phase 3\n1475\trather than assumed. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\n1476\tauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n1477\t\n1478\t### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n1479\t\n1480\t**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\n1481\tresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n1482\t\n1483\tBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\n1484\twhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Two ways out:\n1485\t\n1486\t1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n1487\t   stays untouched.\n1488\t2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n1489\t   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n1490\t   everything after it.\n1491\t\n1492\tOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\n1493\twhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\n1494\tnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n1495\t\n1496\t---\n1497\t\n1498\t## 21. Testing strategy and quality gates\n\n### 14.1 Tiers\n\n| Tier | What | Runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. It\n> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n\n### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n\n**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\nrejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\nround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\nincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\nthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n\n### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n\nShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n\n- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n\n### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n\nCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\nincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\ndoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\nexecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n\n### 14.5 Quality gates\n\n| Gate | Requirement |\n|---|---|\n| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. This exists because every critical defect found in review was a bookkeeping failure attached to correct reasoning; making the numbers executable removes the class |\n\n**All-gates-same-commit:** G1–G4 and **G7** MUST pass on the *same* commit — these are\nfast. G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build; G6 is release-only. A green build\nassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n\n### 14.6 Definition of done\n\nA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G5 are green on one commit; every\nnew failure mode has a test; every new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan\nis updated if any decision changed.\n\n**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\na data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\ntell what they are running).\n\n---\n\n## 15. Throughput expectations\n\n*Forecasts from research. The committed numbers are §13.1.*\n\n| Stage | Approach | Expected | Regime |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| — | Single QR (what most projects do) | 1–9 KB/s | handheld, matches TXQR |\n| **1** | **Tiled monochrome QR** | **20–45 KB/s** | tripod, laptop→phone |\n| **2** | **+ RGB channel tripling** | **35–90 KB/s** | tripod |\n| **3** | **libcimbar-derived codec** | **~106 KB/s** | libcimbar's published figure, monitor→phone. **Its advantage is frame rate, not density** — see below |\n| — | Phone-to-phone research SOTA | ~40 KB/s | lab, mounted |\n| — | All-time lab record (PixNet) | 12 Mb/s | **30\" LCD + 24 MP DSLR — not comparable** |\n\n**Stage 3's rationale — corrected.** An earlier revision of this section claimed *\"QR is denser\nper pixel than libcimbar\"* (0.0794 vs 0.0741 bits/screen px²) and used it to push symbology to\nlast place. **That comparison was invalid, and in exactly the way AP1 warns about:** the 0.0794\nfigure is QR v16-L at **3** screen px/module, below this plan's own ≥ 4 camera px/module decode\nfloor. Compared at a size that actually decodes:\n\n| Scheme | Bits per screen px² (at its decode floor) |\n|---|---|\n| QR v16-L @ **4** px/module | **0.0447** |\n| libcimbar, 6 bits over 9×9 px | **0.0741** |\n| *(QR v16-L @ 3 px/module — below the floor, not comparable)* | *0.0794* |\n\n**libcimbar is ~1.66× denser per pixel at a decodable cell size**, and it also sustains ~11\ndecoded frames/s where the rig managed 2–4. So its advantage is **both** density and frame\nrate, and Stage 3 is *more* attractive than the corrected-away version suggested — not less.\n\nWhat survives from that reasoning: **decode CPU per bit is the metric that matters**, and the\ncheap decode-side wins (worker pool, tight ROI, capture resolution, D27) come first because\nthey are cheap, not because symbology is worthless. **R7 (MPL-2.0 licensing) and §19 Q1 are\ntherefore NOT de-urgentised** — they gate Phase 7 and Phase 7 is worth reaching.\n\n**The dominant risk is geometry, not software.** Cell size is set by how many *camera\npixels* the sender's screen occupies:\n\n- Laptop → phone at 30 cm: ~1325 px across ≈ 165-cell grid\n- **Phone → phone: ~327 px across ≈ 54 cells — one ninth the capacity**\n\nPhone→phone is also bounded by **minimum focus distance**: filling the frame needs ~6.6 cm,\ninside the ~10 cm focus limit, so the symbol spans only 50–60% of frame.\n\n---\n\n## 16. Platform and operations\n\n### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n\n- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n\n### 16.2 Deployment\n\nStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\nNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n\n### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n\nTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\na service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\nbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n\n| Rule | |\n|---|---|\n| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n\n### 16.4 Health check\n\nOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\nthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\nlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n\n---\n\n## 17. Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | Sustained fps decline > 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and **tell the user**, rather than silently running hot and slow. If duty-cycling cannot hold the rate, reframe multi-GB as a multi-session workflow (§1.1) |\n\n---\n\n## 18.1 Anti-patterns — mistakes this project has already made\n\nEvery entry below was made *in this repo* and cost real time. They are collected here because\neach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\nstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n\n| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n\n## 18.2 Proof obligations\n\nEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\nbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n\n| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n\n## 19. Open questions\n\n1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Porting is legal but makes the repo\n   mixed-license and obliges per-file marking. The failure mode is someone pasting in a\n   function and deciding this by accident. → [`prior-art-libcimbar.md`](../notes/prior-art-libcimbar.md)\n2. **Optimal K and block size on real hardware.** §3.1 is a model, not a measurement.\n   Resolve in Phase 1 (R1).\n3. **Phone→phone viability** at 54 cells. Resolve in Phase 3 (R4).\n4. **Progress UX with no back-channel.** The sender cannot know receiver progress. Over a\n   10-hour transfer this matters far more than over 30 seconds. **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n5. **Should the sender ever stop?** It loops forever; at GB scale \"forever\" may be days.\n   **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n6. **Delta transfer vs fixed blocks** — see §20.2. **Resolve before Phase 4 implementation.**\n7. **Closed-loop negotiation — deferred on evidence.** Bidirectional links are precedented\n   (MAMBA: two phones, 11–28 kbps each way), but MAMBA's measured gain from closing the\n   loop is only **5–20%**, while changing the coding paradigm buys multiples. Reassess\n   after Phase 4. → [`link-adaptation-design.md`](../notes/link-adaptation-design.md)\n8. **SoftLight-style soft hints — the highest-ceiling idea we are not doing.** Per-bit\n   confidence plus a false-positive-tolerant rateless code: **2.2× with fixed parameters**.\n   Blocked on zxing returning hard bytes; natural fit for Stage 3.\n9. **Multi-GB export on iOS** (R5). Detect up front, never at hour 9.\n10. **Encryption.** Out of scope for v1 (T6), but the optical channel is uniquely exposed\n    to filming. Revisit once transport is real.\n\n---\n\n## 20. Adopted roadmap items\n\nFrom [`ideas-ledger.md`](../notes/ideas-ledger.md) (103 generated → 10 finalists → 7\nadopted). Tracked as beads blocking genesis `bf-28p`.\n\n| Bead | Item | Grade | Phase |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `bf-4d6` | Storage pre-flight and capacity gate | S | 4 |\n| `bf-5vm` | Diagnostic stall detector | M | 5 |\n| `bf-1g0` | Aim reticle and distance coach | M | 5 |\n| `bf-6d3` | Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1) | S | 5 |\n| `bf-280` | Delta transfer and cross-session resume | L | 4+ |\n| `bf-4tb` | Pairing splash QR | S | 5 |\n| `bf-13h` | Verifiable build + version footer | M | 0 |\n\n**Rejected:** *text/secret fast path* (a different product inside this one) and\n*single-file HTML build* (deploying as a static site, and WASM is required — exactly what\nsingle-file cannot cleanly inline). The PWA offline story is unaffected.\n\n### 20.1 Photosensitivity changes a rendering decision (`bf-6d3`)\n\nWCAG 2.3.1 caps general flashes at three per second **or** requires the flashing area to\nstay under the small-safe threshold. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\nhours is a genuine seizure risk.\n\n**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\nfewer cells → less throughput. The compliant design is therefore **a bounded coded region\ninside a static surround**, not full-bleed, and the area cost MUST be measured in Phase 3\nrather than assumed. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\nauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n\n### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n\n**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\nresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n\nBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\nwhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Two ways out:\n\n1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n   stays untouched.\n2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n   everything after it.\n\nOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\nwhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\nnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n\n---\n\n## 21.
